exercises.heading: 6.5. Exercises
exercises.instruction: 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, and 8 Find the average value of the function on the given interval.

problem.paragraph: $${f(x)} = 3x^{2} + 8x$$ , $$\left\lbrack {- 1,2} \right\rbrack$$
$${f(x)} = \sqrt{x}$$ , $$\left\lbrack {0,4} \right\rbrack$$
$$g(x) = 3\cos x$$ , $$\left\lbrack {- \pi \slash 2,\pi \slash 2} \right\rbrack$$
$$f(z) = \frac{e^{1/z}}{z^{2}}$$ , $$\left\lbrack {1,4} \right\rbrack$$
$${f(x)} = \frac{x^{2}}{\left( {x^{3} + 3} \right)^{2}}$$ , $$\left\lbrack {- 1,1} \right\rbrack$$
$$h(x) = \cos^{4}x\sin x$$ , $$\left\lbrack {0,\pi} \right\rbrack$$
$$h(u) = \frac{\ln u}{u}$$ , $$\left\lbrack {1,5} \right\rbrack$$

exercises.instruction: 9, 10, 11, and 12 Find the average value of $$f$$ on the given interval. Find $$c$$ in the given interval such that $$f_{avg} = {f(c)}$$ . Sketch the graph of $$f$$ and a rectangle whose base is the given interval and whose area is the same as the area under the graph of $$f$$ .

problem.paragraph: $${f(t)} = 1/t^{2}$$ , $$\left\lbrack {1,3} \right\rbrack$$
$$g(x) = (x + 1)^{3}$$ , $$\left\lbrack {0,2} \right\rbrack$$
$${f(x)} = 2\sin x - \sin 2x$$ , $$\left\lbrack {0,\pi} \right\rbrack$$
$${f(x)} = 2xe^{- x^{2}}$$ , $$\left\lbrack {0,2} \right\rbrack$$
If $$f$$ is continuous and $$\int_{1}^{3}{{f(x)}dx = 8}$$ , show that $$f$$ takes on the value $$4$$ at least once on the interval $$\left\lbrack {1,3} \right\rbrack$$ .
Find the numbers $$b$$ such that the average value of $${f(x)} = 2 + 6x - 3x^{2}$$ on the interval $$\left\lbrack {0,b} \right\rbrack$$ is equal to $$3$$ .
Find the average value of $$f$$ on $$\left\lbrack {0,8} \right\rbrack$$ .

image.alt: Details A function is graphed on the x y coordinate plane. The x axis is displayed from 0 to 8 in increments of 2, and the y axis from negative 1 to 3, in increments of 1. The function begins at (0, -1), rises linearly up and to the right until (2, 1), slopes downward to the right until (3, 0), slopes upward until (4, 2), and runs horizontally until (6, 2), dips to (5, 1) and then rises to (8, 3).

problem.paragraph: The velocity graph of an accelerating car is shown.

image.alt: Details A curve is graphed on the first quadrant of a coordinate plane. The horizontal axis is labeled t and is displayed from 0 to 12 seconds in increments of 2 seconds. The vertical axis is labeled v and is displayed from 0 to 60 kilometers per hour in increments of 20 kilometers per hour. The curve begins at the origin, goes up to the right, concave down, until (12, 70), passing through approximately (2, 20), (6, 50).

list.item: Use the Midpoint Rule to estimate the average velocity of the car during the first $$12$$ seconds.
At what time was the instantaneous velocity equal to the average velocity?

problem.paragraph: In a certain city the temperature (in $${}_{}^{}{}$$ ) $$t$$ hours after 9 am was modeled by the function
Find the average temperature during the period from 9 am to 9 pm.

The figure shows graphs of the temperatures for a city on the East Coast and a city on the West Coast during a $$24$$ -hour period starting at midnight. Which city had the highest temperature that day? Find the average temperature during this time period for each city using the Midpoint Rule with $$n = 12$$ . Interpret your results; which city was “warmer” overall that day?

image.alt: Details Two curves are graphed on the first quadrant of a coordinate plane. The horizontal axis is labeled t, displayed from 0 to 24 hours in increments of 1 hour. The vertical axis is labeled T and displayed from 40 to 80 degrees Fahrenheit in increments of 10 degrees. both the curves have mild fluctuations throughout their path. The curve labeled West Coast begins slightly below 55 degrees on the T axis, and passes through the approximate points (1, 65), (3, 55), (5, 50), (7, 55), (8, 54), (9, 60), (11, 65), (13, 80), (15, 65), (17, 60), (19, 55), (20, 48), (21, 50), (22, 48), (23, 50), and exits at approximately (24, 46). The curve labeled East Coast begins slightly below 60 on the T axis and, passes through the approximate points (2, 63), (3, 60), (5, 65), (7, 63), (9, 75), (10, 65), (11, 70), (13, 65), (15, 70), (16, 69), (17, 55), (18, 56), (19, 65), (21, 60), (22, 60), (23, 55), and exits at approximately (24, 57).

problem.paragraph: The linear density in a rod $$8$$ m long is $$12 \slash \sqrt{x + 1}{kg} \slash m$$ , where $$x$$ is measured in meters from one end of the rod. Find the average density of the rod.
The velocity $$\upsilon$$ of blood that flows in a blood vessel with radius $$R$$ and length $$l$$ at a distance $$r$$ from the central axis is
$$\upsilon(r) = \frac{P}{4\eta l}\left( {R^{2} - r^{2}} \right)$$

where $$P$$ is the pressure difference between the ends of the vessel and $$\eta$$ is the viscosity of the blood (see Example 3.7.7). Find the average velocity (with respect to $$r$$ ) over the interval $$0 \leqslant r \leqslant R$$ . Compare the average velocity with the maximum velocity.

In Example 3.8.1 we modeled the world population in the second half of the $$20$$ th century by the equation $$P(t) = 2560e^{0.017185t}$$ . Use this equation to estimate the average world population during this time period (1950–2000).

list.item: A cup of coffee has temperature $$95{}_{}^{}$$ and takes $$30$$ minutes to cool to $$61{}_{}^{}$$ in a room with temperature $$20{}_{}^{}$$ . Use Newton’s Law of Cooling (Section 3.8) to show that the temperature of the coffee after $$t$$ minutes is $${T(t)} = 20 + 75e^{- kt}$$ where $$k \approx 0.02$$ .
What is the average temperature of the coffee during the first half hour?

problem.paragraph: Use the result of Exercise 5.5.89 to compute the average volume of inhaled air in the lungs in one respiratory cycle.

If a freely falling body starts from rest, then its displacement is given by $$s = \frac{1}{2}gt^{2}$$ . Let the velocity after a time $$T$$ be $$\upsilon_{T}$$ . Show that if we compute the average of the velocities with respect to $$t$$ we get $$\upsilon_{avg} = \frac{1}{2}\upsilon_{T}$$ , but if we compute the average of the velocities with respect to $$s$$ we get $$\upsilon_{avg} = \frac{2}{3}\upsilon_{T}$$ .
Use the diagram to show that if $$f$$ is concave upward on $$\left\lbrack {a,b} \right\rbrack$$ , then
$$f_{avg} > {f\left( \frac{a + b}{2} \right)}$$

image.alt: Details A curve, a line, and four-line segments are graphed on the x y coordinate plane. There are three tick marks on the x axis: a, (a + b)/2, and b. The curve begins directly above the tick mark a, goes up to the right, and concaves up until it is directly above the tick mark b. The line is tangent to the curve at about half its length. From the tick mark b, a vertical line segment rises upward to meet the curve. From the tick mark (a + b)/2, a vertical line segment rises upward to meet the curve and the line at the point of tangency. From the tick mark a, a vertical line segment rises upward to the same height as the point of tangency. A horizontal line segment connects the line segment from a to the one from b.

exercises.instruction: 26–27 Let $$f_{avg}\lbrack a,b\rbrack$$ denote the average value of $$f$$ on the interval $$\lbrack a,b\rbrack$$ .

problem.paragraph: Show that if $$a < c < b$$ , then
$$f_{avg}\lbrack a,b\rbrack = \left( \frac{c - a}{b - a} \right)f_{avg}\lbrack a,c\rbrack + \left( \frac{b - c}{b - a} \right)f_{avg}\lbrack c,b\rbrack$$
Show that if $$f$$ is continuous, then $$\lim_{t\rightarrow a^{+}}f_{avg}\lbrack a,t\rbrack = f(a)$$ .
Prove the Mean Value Theorem for Integrals by applying the Mean Value Theorem for derivatives (see Section 4.2) to the function $$F(x) = {\int_{a}^{x}{f(t)dt}}$$ .
